stimulus.source_note: Photograph: crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival, August 15, 1969, by Derek Redmond and Paul Campbell, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Attendance figures verified against Britannica and the Smithsonian; Altamont account verified against Britannica and Library of Congress accounts.
stimulus.text:
The photograph, taken on August 15, 1969, shows part of the huge crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival on a dairy farm in Bethel, New York. More than 400,000 young people gathered for three days of rock music. The promoters had told local officials to expect no more than 50,000 people.

Four months later, in December 1969, promoters tried to repeat Woodstock with a free festival at the Altamont Speedway in California. The event was disorganized, the Hells Angels motorcycle club served as security, and a concertgoer, Meredith Hunter, was stabbed and killed during the Rolling Stones’ set.

stem: The size of the Woodstock crowd best shows which change in American culture by 1969?

options.text: Rock music had faded as a youth interest
options.misconception: A crowd of more than 400,000 shows rock interest growing, not fading.

options.text: Most young people had returned to the music of the 1950s
options.misconception: The crowd came for the rock acts of 1969.

options.text: Youth culture had become a mass audience for the music business
Live concerts had been replaced by television shows
options.misconception: Woodstock was a live festival, not a television show.

rationales.A: More than 400,000 young people gathered for three days of rock music, the opposite of fading interest.
rationales.B: The crowd gathered for the rock acts of 1969, not for the music of the 1950s.
rationales.C: The promoters expected 50,000 and more than 400,000 came: the youth audience was far larger than anyone in the business had planned for.
rationales.D: The passage describes a live festival of more than 400,000 people, not a television show.
rationales.general:
1. The promoters planned for no more than 50,000 people.
2. More than 400,000 came, about eight times the expected crowd.
3. A crowd that size is a market: promoters, record companies, and radio could all sell to it.
4. Youth culture had grown from a scene into a mass audience.
Remember: When the crowd dwarfs the plan, the audience has outgrown the business built for it.
